title: Event-conditioned isotope renewal in an ideal model with decisive physical gates open
reported_status: Conditional internal mathematical/model construction only. The nominal 90% values are expectations at planning p=.01109 and central 95 kV cross sections sigma_L=56.6 mb, sigma_H=2.1 mb; retry/dose tails are unbounded and finite caps reduce yield. They are not a general 90% cost. The blind-dose theorem does not cover outcome-dependent stopping. Same-atom event/reset/protection and material response are not demonstrated; no experiment was performed.

scientific_scope_status: At fixed deterministic cumulative fluence per attempted site and unconditioned occupied output, the blind writer has q*=p sigma_L/[p sigma_L+(1-p)sigma_H], while vacancy-history stopping is informative and outside that quantifier. In the ideal renewal, irradiate one fresh atom until ejection or screening fluence d; an ejection triggers independent fresh refill/restart, while a complete survivor is accepted and protected. Then q(d)=p exp(-sigma_H d)/[p exp(-sigma_H d)+(1-p)exp(-sigma_L d)]. At planning p=.01109 and central 95 kV cross sections sigma_L=56.6 mb and sigma_H=2.1 mb, the nominal 90% calculation gives EXPECTED costs of about 105 attempts, 104 refills and 1.959e13 target electrons/nm^2. Retry and dose tails are unbounded; finite caps reduce yield. These are conditional expectations at those inputs, not a general 90% cost. 0.298 J/nm^2 is incident kinetic energy per uniformly addressed area, not absorbed heat, per-site energy or wall-plug cost. Same-atom no-ejection record, independent fresh refill/composition, preserved repaired-site rates, neighbor protection, event/reset and final readout are unacquired.
